source.title: Refusal Boundaries in Language Models Overindex on Superficial Linguistic Cues
source.authors: Meru Gopalan; Alec Harris; Kartik Goyal

record.file_problem: None apparent; full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests causal activation addition and ablation of difference-of-means refusal directions, but uses refusal-defined and paired-rewrite directions rather than the original harmful-minus-harmless direction and does not reproduce the original intervention exactly.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports attacker-training results using refusal signals as rewards, but those behaviors are deliberately optimized for and do not test whether the signal itself mediates naturally occurring refusal. It cites multi-direction refusal work but does not test affine or cone structure. The Layer 12 harmful–harmless vector is used as an optimization objective, not as a direct causal intervention.
record.test_reason: Ablates and adds difference-of-means refusal directions in Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-32B and measures refusal rates. The directions are refused-minus-answered and paired-rewrite displacements, not the original harmful-minus-harmless direction, so this is a different method aimed at V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but misplaces the emphasis. The main conclusion is that refusal boundaries overindex on superficial cues, shown by cue insertion, and that refusal signals equivalent for classification diverge under optimization. On directions, the authors say abliterating general over-refusal directions cuts false refusals with no detectable AdvBench safety loss, and that addition induces refusal in both models. They add that the Qwen direction was not shown necessary and that directions are not category-specific.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-of-means activation directions and causal additions/ablations, but most causal directions are defined from refused versus answered prompts or paired rewrites rather than harmful versus harmless instructions. The study tests selected layers and settings rather than the original formulation as a whole.
record.method_sensitivity: The causal direction and its effect vary by model and layer: Llama Layer 17 was selected for causal effects; Qwen Layer 58 induced refusal but was not shown necessary, and Layers 57–61 performed similarly. Abliterated category directions also had different relative effects across Llama and Qwen.

fits_no_version.finding: Inserting superficial cues (touchy subjects, character noise, combined cues) into benign prompts raises over-refusal, with effects that vary by model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superficial lexical and format cues causally raise over-refusal in safety-tuned LLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual directions orthogonal to the overall displacement direction reduce over-refusal, in Llama more than d1 does (33.0 vs 6.6 pp). Their relative strengths are not consistent across models, and they are not category-specific.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Over-refusal can be reduced by ablating several non-category-specific directions beyond the main refusal displacement.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal vectors that predict and causally control refusal are poor optimization rewards for natural-language rewrites (Table 1); only the refusal-prefix reward beats its baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal signals with similar classification performance diverge under optimization pressure.

record.problems: The study covers two models and predominantly English, single-turn prompts. Its safety-cost assessment is limited to 200 AdvBench prompts and cannot rule out smaller or out-of-distribution costs. The authors note judge and semantic-equivalence limitations, exploratory overlapping cue categories, and that Qwen's low-baseline diagnostic ablation limits the necessity test.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 contains additional cue-category and combined-cue values not individually reported in the text; they are omitted rather than transcribed from the plot. Figure 3 also marks coercion and fabrication as not in Llama's frame set; no result row is reported for those Llama conditions.

untested.parts: No causal ablation or addition of the original harmful-minus-harmless direction; the Layer 12 harmful-harmless direction is used only as an optimization objective. No general-capability evaluation.
Abliteration is an activation-level projection. There is no weight edit and no evaluation of released abliterated models.
Gradient jailbreaks are not analysed for direction suppression, and there is no adversarial training.
No affine, cone or multi-direction test of refusal.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
The Llama-defined prompt classes are reused for Qwen, but no direction-transfer test is run.
Qwen3 thinking mode is not analysed; no reasoning-model test.

missing.what: Per-direction harmful-refusal-lost values, especially for the refused-minus-nonrefused vector in each model.
Statement that no Qwen candidate layer worked well under abliteration.
Pre-ablation refusal rate on the 400 held-out over-refusals, needed to express removal as a fraction of refusals.
Apparent discrepancy between L17 removal cutting harmful refusal to 83% (diagnostic set) and no AdvBench decrease after every-layer abliteration.

record.verdict_notes: Rows r1–r4 come from layer selection, so they are optimistic. The every-layer abliteration of the refusal vector leaving harmful refusal intact is the most direct V1 evidence here, and it cuts against V1. It concerns a refused-minus-nonrefused direction, not Arditi's harmful-minus-harmless one. The reader mislabelled r20/r21 as a safety-preservation pass.

versions.untested_parts: Does not causally ablate and add the same harmful-minus-harmless direction. Does not test simultaneous removal of that direction at every layer and position, or general capabilities; harmful-prompt refusal is the only reported safety-cost check.
No conversion of activation ablation into a weight edit or evaluation of released abliteration edits.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
Does not test affine, cone, or dominant-plus-additional-direction accounts of refusal.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or systematic model-variant transfer test of a direction.
Does not vary how or when refusal training occurs.

source_check.notes: The pack listed verdicts without [lN] ids, so I numbered them l1-l4 in pack order. The refused-nonrefused vector comes from S-Eval/Anthropic red-team/Onepane prompts split by Llama's refusal, not from rewrites. Llama L17 removal 99->83% (selection-stage) sits in tension with no AdvBench decrease under every-layer abliteration. The Qwen diagnostic removal 2%->7% isn't among the checked rows.

statements.correction: Refused-nonrefused vector: class-mean difference (2,500 prompts per class) of S-Eval, Anthropic red-team and Onepane.ai prompts split by Llama-3-8B-Instruct's measured refusal; Qwen reuses the classes. Abliterated (activation projection) at every layer: no detected decrease on 200 AdvBench prompts in either model. Qwen unabliterated 99%; Llama AdvBench baseline not stated.
statements.problem: Says the refused-minus-nonrefused direction comes from over-refusal rewrites. It does not: only d1 and the cluster directions come from rewrite pairs.
